feature: Universal audio device routing for Floating Athena

architecture.discovery: Chromium MediaDevices over native macOS Core Audio / Windows audio endpoints; one visible discovery broker: Floating Athena when shown, otherwise the control window. Event-driven device changes, without polling processes or extra dependencies.
architecture.authority: Validated main-process IPC stores runtime inventory, resolves routing, gates microphone tests, and holds output after a route change. Preferences use the existing settings repository.
architecture.microphone: Selected physical input, shared constraints with echo cancellation/noise suppression, serialized capture, late-open cleanup, bounded reconnect attempts, and event-triggered recovery when no microphone exists at startup. Existing Silero/Whisper pipeline and voice session remain in use.
architecture.output: Each utterance pins HTMLAudioElement and the avatar Web Audio analyser to the same physical output. Changed/missing output stops playback and requires explicit confirmation; interrupted speech is not replayed.
architecture.privacy: No raw microphone audio, transcript, device identifier or screen contents in this report. Microphone tests retain RMS only. OS permission, app opt-in and capture leases remain enforced.

confirmed_previous_defects: Wake capture always selected the system default; an ended track permanently stopped the listener.
Speech elements had no output selection; avatar amplitude processing separately routed sound to AudioContext default output.
Voice settings had no persistent device override or bounded microphone meter test.

limitations: AirPods and other Bluetooth devices were not physically available; Bluetooth profile changes use the same endpoint lifecycle but are not hardware-verified here.
No Windows machine or macOS Intel hardware was available. The Chromium routing path is shared, but Windows/Intel production builds and hardware were not live-tested.
Microphone identities may be hidden until authorized capture. Voice Settings explains this and provides Test microphone; no automatic microphone capture is performed merely to reveal labels.
OS drivers control Bluetooth codec/profile quality; Athena does not force high-quality stereo while a hands-free microphone is active.
Hardware echo cancellation and noise suppression vary by device; a bounded recent-playback transcript guard supplements them.
Apple notarization requires deployment credentials and was not performed; local macOS packaging uses the existing persistent signing certificate.
app_restart: Verified normal packaged Athena quit and restarted (PID 12726 → 38529). Voice Settings displays Audio Devices, System Default input/output, automatic switching on and AB17X USB output. Existing hands-free-off preference retained; no other applications were stopped.
